messages:
maya: Heads up — CI is red on build #482. Intermittent failure in runtime/executor: TestExecutorShutdownRace. Fails ~3/10 runs.
ci-bot: Build #482 FAILED — https://ci.internal/reports/482
maya: Pasted the failing log below. Happening during teardown, looks like goroutine leak + panic in shutdown path:
```
--- FAIL: TestExecutorShutdownRace (0.04s)
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
goroutine 45 [running]:
runtime/debug.Stack()
    /usr/local/go/src/runtime/debug/stack.go:24 +0x65
internal/executor.(*Executor).Shutdown(0xc00012a000)
    /repo/runtime/executor/executor.go:312 +0x2a4
runtime_test.TestExecutorShutdownRace(0xc0000a8000)
    /repo/runtime/executor/executor_test.go:87 +0x15f
```
maya: The failing line is Shutdown calling into scheduler; sometimes scheduler already nil.
@tomas can you bisect? This started after the scheduler refactor last week.

tomas: On it. Can you add the build id and failing commit? I need the exact commit hash from that CI run.
maya: Build shows commit `3f7b2d1` (merge/refactor-scheduler). Also saw a similar stack when running with `-race` locally once.

rachel: My hunch is a scheduling/timer race where Stop() races with the periodic heartbeat goroutine. We added more goroutine handoff in that refactor.
jen: If it's a heartbeat/timer race we might be able to reproduce by controlling time in tests (fake clock) instead of sleeps.

omar: Agree with fake clock approach. Adding sleeps is flaky. For quick triage, can we rerun CI to see variability frequency?
maya: Triggering rerun — @ci-bot can you rerun just that test on the same agent set? /rerun --test TestExecutorShutdownRace
ci-bot: Rerun requested: Build #483 queued (targeting same agents as #482). Will report when done.

ci-bot: Build #483 COMPLETE — PASS
maya: Passed once. Still concerned. Tomas, can you try `-count=100` locally to stress it?

tomas: Running stress now: `go test ./runtime/executor -run TestExecutorShutdownRace -count 100 -race`
(takes a few minutes)

tomas: Reproduced locally on iteration 42 with race detector. Attached local trace excerpt above. Looks like shutdown path doesn't acquire the scheduler lock in one ordering.

rachel: Can you paste the small repro snippet? If we can make a deterministic interleaving we can add a targeted unit test and fix.

maya: Minimal repro in a gist: start executor, start heartbeat goroutine, call Shutdown concurrently with a Cancel on ctx. Non-deterministic when scheduler pointer gets cleared.

omar: Quick mitigation: add nil check in Shutdown to avoid panic and log a debug warning. Not ideal but reduces noise while we root cause.
jen: I'd prefer a test-first fix: add a deterministic test that forces the timing by hooking the scheduler with channels to control handoff.

tomas: I'll open a PR with two commits: (1) test harness that can reproduce the failure reliably by blocking/unblocking the heartbeat, (2) fix to proper lock ordering in Shutdown. If we need a short-term mitigation, include the nil-check but mark as temporary with comment and issue link.

maya: Sounds good. Please add `bisect-needed` label and link the failing build in the PR description. Also add `flaky:investigate` tag so test flakiness dashboard picks it up.

tomas: PR draft up: https://git.internal/redwood/rt/+/PR-227 — includes logs and reproducer. Marked WIP.

rachel: Quick review note — don't swallow errors in Shutdown. If we add a nil-check, at least emit a metric so we can alert if it happens in prod.

jen: :thumbsup: will review PR tomorrow morning.

ci-bot: FYI — I scheduled a nightly stress job for this test group to run 500 iterations for 24 hours. Will file a summary.

maya: Thanks all. Will follow up in the PR. If someone reproduces a different failure mode ping here.
